_comment: One-way door rules. A match makes the agent stop and ask a human. Override or extend per user (~/.sharp/one-way-doors.json) or per project (.sharp/one-way-doors.json); a rule with the same id and "disabled": true turns one off. Keep this list short: a gate that fires constantly trains people to click yes without reading.

rules.title: Destructive database statement
rules.why: Deleted rows and dropped tables are gone unless a recent backup exists, and restoring a backup also loses everything written since.
rules.blast: Every user and service that reads this data.
rules.safer: Rename or soft-delete first, take a fresh backup, or run inside a transaction you can roll back.

rules.title: Destructive migration written
rules.why: Writing the file is reversible. Applying it deletes data for good.
rules.blast: Production data and any service or report still reading the column or table.
rules.safer: Expand/contract: stop writing, deploy, verify nothing reads it, then drop in a later release.

rules.title: Apply a migration that drops data
rules.why: This migration drops a column or table, so the data in it is gone once it's applied (unless there's a backup).
rules.blast: Everything that reads the dropped column or table, and its stored data.
rules.safer: Back up the table first, or expand/contract: stop using it, deploy, then drop it in a later release.

rules.title: Force-push to a shared branch
rules.why: It rewrites history that teammates and CI have already pulled, and their commits can silently disappear.
rules.blast: Everyone who has this branch checked out.
rules.safer: Push a new branch and open a PR, or use git revert instead of rewriting history.

rules.title: Discard uncommitted work
rules.why: Uncommitted and untracked changes were never saved in git, so nothing can bring them back.
rules.safer: git stash -u first, or commit to a scratch branch.

rules.title: Recursive delete
rules.why: Files deleted this way skip the trash and can't be recovered without a backup.
rules.safer: List what would be deleted first (ls or find), or move it to a backup folder.

rules.title: Delete or replace cloud infrastructure
rules.why: Deleted cloud resources such as disks, buckets and databases often take their data with them, and an apply can replace resources in place.
rules.blast: Every service running on this infrastructure.
rules.safer: Run plan or preview first and read the diff, and snapshot any stateful resources.

rules.title: Production deploy
rules.why: Real users see the change immediately, and a rollback can't undo emails sent, data written, or what users saw in the meantime.
rules.safer: Deploy to staging first, use a canary or feature flag, and know your rollback command.

rules.title: Publish a package or release
rules.why: A published version number is permanent: registries block re-use, and others may already have downloaded it.
rules.blast: Everyone who depends on this package.
rules.safer: Publish a pre-release tag (for example -rc.1) or run a dry run first.

rules.title: Delete or expose a repository
rules.why: Deleting a repo destroys its issues and PRs. Making it public exposes all of its history, including any secret ever committed.
rules.blast: The whole team, and possibly the public.
rules.safer: Archive instead of deleting, and scan the history for secrets before changing visibility.

rules.title: Send a message outside the team
rules.why: A sent message cannot be unsent.
rules.safer: Show the human the exact text and recipient list first.

rules.title: Irreversible action through a connected tool
rules.why: Connected tools act on real systems, such as email, payments or tickets, outside this workspace.
rules.blast: People and systems outside this session.
rules.safer: Draft it and let the human send or approve it.

rules.title: Change the project license
rules.why: Code already released under the old license stays under it, so this is a legal commitment.
rules.safer: Get explicit sign-off from the project owner or legal.
